name: Early Training Evaluation of Small Language Models
description: This task focuses on designing evaluation benchmarks to assess the early training progress of small language models (SLMs) in acquiring scientific knowledge, reasoning, and other capabilities.

cr:input.name: Pre-trained Small Language Models and Checkpoints
cr:input.description: Three pre-trained small language models (0.5B, 1B, and 3B parameters) with intermediate checkpoints sampled during training up to 200 billion tokens. Models are trained on two data mixtures: a web-only dataset and a scientific knowledge dataset.

cr:input.contentUrl: [FILL IN THE BLANK: dataset download URL]

cr:output.name: predictions
cr:output.description: The expected output includes performance signals that measure the early training progress of SLMs. These signals should reflect the models' ability to acquire scientific knowledge and reasoning capabilities.

field.name: model_size
field.description: The size of the model being evaluated (e.g., 0.5B, 1B, 3B).

field.name: training_tokens
field.description: The number of training tokens processed (e.g., 50 billion, 100 billion).

field.name: benchmark_score
field.description: The performance score on the evaluation benchmark (e.g., MMLU-var score).

cr:evaluation.notes: Metrics evaluate the ability of SLMs to acquire scientific knowledge and reasoning capabilities during early training. MMLU-var is highlighted as a more effective benchmark for early-stage evaluation.

open_questions: What specific evaluation metrics should be used to measure the quality of performance signals?
How can benchmarks be refined to better capture intermediate reasoning capabilities?
